'''Idah Sithole-Niang''' (born 1957) is a Zimbabwean [[biochemist]] and educator. Her main area of research has been viruses which attack the [[cowpea]], one of the major food crops of [[Zimbabwe]].

==Biography==
Idah Sithole was born in [[Hwange]], [[Zimbabwe]], on 2 October 1957. She attended the [[University of London]], on scholarship, earning a BS in biochemistry in 1982.{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=273}} When she was awarded a [[USAID]] Fellowship in 1983,{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=274}} Sithole chose to continue her education, studying plant and virus genetics. She earned a PhD in 1988 from [[Michigan State University]] (MSU) in [[Lansing, Michigan]].{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=273}} She completed a post-doctoral fellowship at the Plant Research Laboratory at MSU researching the genetics of photosynthesis in [[cyanobacteria]]<ref name="African Agricultural Technology Foundation">{{cite web|title=Idah Sithole-Niang|url=http://www.aatf-africa.org/about-us/governance/board-trustees/idah-sithole-niang|publisher=African Agricultural Technology Foundation|access-date=11 November 2015|location=Nairobi, Kenya|date=2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120212908/http://www.aatf-africa.org/about-us/governance/board-trustees/idah-sithole-niang|archive-date=20 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> on the first William L. Brown Fellowship, awarded by the Resources Development Foundation.<ref name="Brown Fellowship">{{cite journal|last1=Cunningham|first1=Isabel Shipley|title=William Lacy Brown 1913-1991: Scientist, Executive & Mentor: He Left a Lasting Legacy to Global Agriculture|journal=Diversity|date=1992|volume=8|issue=2|page=21|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/Portals/0/wlbc/PDF's/vol8_2.pdf|access-date=11 November 2015|publisher=Genetic Resources Communications Systems, Inc.|location=Washington, DC|issn=0744-8163}}</ref> Returning to Zimbabwe, she became a [[Lecturer]] at the University of Zimbabwe in 1992 on viruses which infect plants. Her chief area of research is the [[potyvirus]], which attacks the cowpea, a [[legume]] which is a chief food crop of Zimbabwe.{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=273}} That same year, she married Sheikh Ibrahima Niang, a Senegalese professor of anthropology, whom she met at Michigan State University. They have a commuting marriage, as he works at the [[University of Cheikh Anta Diop]] in [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]]. She was awarded a Rockefeller Foundation Fellowship for careers in Biotechnology between 1992 and 1995. She has continued teaching and researching, publishing numerous papers. In 2006 she was made Associate Professor at the University of Zimbabwe.{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=274}}

Sithole-Niang is in favor of genetic modifications to make cowpeas resistant to disease and believes that [[Genetically modified organism|GMO]] versions of traditional crops are beneficial to developing nations. Working with the Network for the Genetic Improvement of Cowpea for Africa (NGICA) as a coordinator, she has consulted with other international experts,{{sfn|Yount|2007|p=274}} in part because of the lack of funding available from within Zimbabwe.<ref name="lack of funding">{{cite news|last1=Tsiko|first1=Sifelani|title=Support for science vital|url=http://southernafrican.news/2015/09/25/support-for-science-vital/|access-date=11 November 2015|publisher=The Southern Times|date=25 September 2015|location=Windhoek, Namibia|archive-date=11 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151111225344/http://southernafrican.news/2015/09/25/support-for-science-vital/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has served as both a member and a board member of numerous organizations including: Steering Committee Trustee of the African Women for Agriculture and Research and Development (AWARD) Programme, the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the American Society for Virologists, Oversight Committee of the Improved Maize for African Soils (IMAS), Selection Committee Chair of the Joshua Nkomo Scholarships, the [[New York Academy of Sciences]], Vice Chair of the Research Council of Zimbabwe, Selection Committee for the Rhodes Scholarships in Zimbabwe and the Zimbabwe Academy of Sciences. Sithole-Niang is a Technical Advisor to the Program for Biosafety Systems for sub-Saharan Africa.<ref name="African Agricultural Technology Foundation" />
